methodSections.heading: Tostones
steps: Heat the oil to 180°C (350°F).
Peel the plantains and cut them into 2-3cm (1in) pieces.
Fry the pieces in the oil until they begin to crisp on the outside.
Let cool for a few minutes, then squash them into medallions using a metal spatula or the bottom of a pan.
Fry these medallions in the oil again until crisp and golden brown.
Season with salt and pepper.

methodSections.heading: Chipotle Aioli
steps: Using an immersion blender, blend both ingredients together.
Chill until served.

methodSections.heading: Media Noche
steps: Preheat a sandwich press to medium hot.
Spread the mayonnaise and Dijon on the cut buns.
Lay the ham slices on the bottom bun then top with the pulled pork.
Add the pickles, followed by the cheese and top half of the bun.
Cook in the sandwich press until the cheese begins to melt and the sandwich is warm throughout.
Serve with tostones and chipotle aioli.

methodSections.heading: Pulled Pork
steps: Preheat the oven to 165°C (325°F). Mix the salt, pepper, and ancho powder.
Score the fatty side of the pork shoulder and rub the spice mixture all over.
Place in a pot suitable for both stove top and oven cooking. Place the sliced fruit, whole peeled garlic, and chopped onions on top of the pork.
Pour the vegetable stock and orange juice into the pot, this should cover three-quarters of the meat.
Bring to a simmer on the stove top then cover and place in the oven at 165°C (325°F) for 6 hours.
Check the pork's internal temperature ensuring it has reached 90°C (190°F).
Remove from the cooking liquid and let cool for a few minutes, then using two forks pull the meat apart.
You will have leftovers for other recipes or it will freeze well too.
